title: Unify batch lanes, remove legacy scheduler threads, and modernize KV cache interfaces
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem summary:

Over the last year we accumulated several overlapping scheduler and batcher implementations: per-model thread pools, multiple batching lanes with duplicated priority logic, and a KV cache API that is tightly coupled to the batcher internals. Under sustained mixed workloads this manifests as high tail latency (p99 increases), uneven GPU utilization, and KV cache lock contention.

Goals:
- Simplify the scheduling surface by consolidating lanes into a single prioritized scheduler with work-stealing between GPU workers.
- Remove the legacy per-model thread pools and replace them with a lightweight task router that respects priority buckets.
- Modernize the KV cache interface: extract a thin trait boundary, implement a sharded eviction backend, and decouple cache warming from the batcher hot-path.
- Upgrade key runtime dependencies (tokio, parking_lot) to pick up bug fixes and better scheduler primitives.

This ticket covers the refactor plan, incremental implementation, and rollout guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: No regression >5% on p99 latency for production chat workload compared to baseline before merge
Achieve >=10% improvement in average GPU token throughput for multi-tenant small-sequence traffic
KV cache lock contention reduced (measured: <25% of requests hitting global mutex wait time)
All existing e2e tests pass and new integration tests for scheduler fairness added
Canary rollout plan defined and exercised in console with automatic rollback on SLO breach
implementation_notes: Design RFC: single scheduler with 3 priority buckets (realtime, interactive, background) and a work-stealing policy for idle workers
Introduce a CacheBackend trait and provide two implementations: sharded in-memory (default) and a future hybrid persistent backend
Replace global KV cache mutex with 16-way sharding keyed by model+prefix hash to avoid hot locks
Bump tokio from 1.22 -> 1.26 and parking_lot to latest patch; validate reactor/timer changes in CI
Break change avoidance: maintain the existing batcher public API while refactoring internals; add compatibility adapter layer for a short transition window
Benchmarks: add microbench for small-sequence bursts and long-context throughput using the internal perf harness
CI: run the runtime perf job on PRs and gate merges if regression >3% for critical workloads

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large refactor could cause temporary throughput regression in some workloads. Mitigation: implement feature-flagged rollout and maintain old batcher adapter behind flag for quick rollback.
Risk: Dependency upgrade exposes subtle behavior changes in timers/sleep. Mitigation: run full CI matrix and add focused integration tests around timeouts and cancellation.

Risk: KV eviction policy changes may affect cold-start latencies. Mitigation: keep current eviction policy semantics for first rollout and only change to LRU/sharded eviction after metrics baseline confirms improvement.
